evals.prompt: Create a new baseapp-frontend package called 'bookmarks' that ships a web and a native bookmark button and reads its data through Relay. Scaffold the package.
evals.expected_output: Should create the eleven always-required files under packages/bookmarks/ plus the Relay and unit-test conditional sets, build with tsc --build tsconfig.build.json, and register the package nowhere else.
assertions: Creates the eleven always-required files under packages/bookmarks/, including tsconfig.build.json, .prettierrc.js, and a CHANGELOG.md seeded with the package-name heading
Sets build to 'rm -rf dist && pnpm relay && tsc --build tsconfig.build.json', the Relay form packages/components/package.json uses, with no bundler step
Copies the scaffold from packages/components or packages/design-system, not from packages/wagtail, whose Cypress setup has no test:component script and whose .gitignore omits /__generated__
Declares a storybook script even with no stories, as packages/provider/package.json does with its 'echo <Name>: No storybook found' stub, so the turbo storybook task has something to run
Does NOT add a tsup.config.ts, and does NOT edit pnpm-workspace.yaml or turbo.json to register the package — the packages/* glob picks the directory up and turbo matches by script name

evals.prompt: I'm writing package.json for the new @baseapp-frontend/bookmarks package. It renders MUI components on web, runs Relay queries, and imports @baseapp-frontend/design-system. What do exports and the dependency sections look like?
evals.expected_output: Should use Shape B — an exports map over TypeScript source subpaths, a files allowlist, and sideEffects: false with no main — and put every runtime library in peerDependencies at a catalog: spec.
assertions: Uses Shape B: an exports map whose targets are TypeScript source subpaths plus a files allowlist covering every target, with no main, no types, and no root index.ts barrel
Writes one exports subpath per module leg — ./bookmarks/common, ./bookmarks/web, ./bookmarks/native — with no directory root and no wildcard, and keeps './package.json': './package.json' in the map

Declares react-native, the three @mui/* packages, react-relay, and relay-runtime under peerDependencies, not dependencies, because a second relay-runtime gives a second store no fragment written against the first can read

Gives @baseapp-frontend/design-system a peerDependencies entry at workspace:*, puts @baseapp-frontend/config, eslint-plugin, and tsconfig in devDependencies, and specs every third-party version as catalog: or a named catalog such as catalog:material-ui

Does NOT pair main: './index.ts' with types: 'dist/index.d.ts' — that is Shape A's defect across authentication, graphql, provider, test, utils, and wagtail, where the two fields disagree about what ships

evals.prompt: Add a 'reactions' module to packages/components. It needs a list component on web and on native, plus one hook both legs share. Lay out the directories and name the files.
evals.expected_output: Should create packages/components/modules/reactions/ with common/, web/, and native/ legs, index.tsx + styled.tsx + types.ts leaves on web, a createStyles() factory on native, and the shared hook under common/hooks/.
assertions: Creates the three legs common/, web/, and native/ under packages/components/modules/reactions/, each with its own index.ts barrel matching one exports subpath
Names every web component leaf index.tsx plus styled.tsx plus types.ts, never <Name>.tsx, and adds constants.ts or utils.ts only when the component needs them
Puts the shared hook at common/hooks/useReactions/ as index.ts plus types.ts exporting UseReactionsOptions and UseReactionsReturn, with the return type annotated on the signature rather than inferred
Has the native leaf export a createStyles() factory returning StyleSheet.create({...}) from styles.ts, not a plain style object, so a call site can pass theme values in later

Models the module on modules/comments and does NOT copy modules/messages or modules/activity-log — messages supplies all thirteen type.ts files and a second __shared__/ per UI leg, and activity-log/native/index.ts is a 0-byte file with a live exports entry

evals.prompt: Our shared upload hook lives in modules/uploads/common/ and I need the file size before uploading. Can I just import expo-file-system there? ESLint isn't complaining.
evals.expected_output: Should reject the expo-file-system import in common/, explain that the restricted-paths zones match file paths and not package specifiers, and move the call into the native leg or behind a headless common/ store.
assertions: Rejects importing expo-file-system from common/, and names messages/common/graphql/mutations/CreateGroupChat.ts as the one file in the tree that already does it and has no resolution on web

Explains that packages/config/.eslintrc-with-restricted-paths.js:6-33 configures import/no-restricted-paths over paths, so a package specifier like expo-file-system or react-native clears every zone and fails at runtime instead of at lint

Keeps the state headless in common/ and renders the surface per platform, or hosts the platform-only affordance in that leg's own context/, or imports the platform package directly inside the platform leg
Notes that common/ must not read process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_* or process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_* either, and routes that through packages/graphql/config/environment.ts instead
Does NOT ship a new .ast-grep rule as part of the block — it recommends the rule as its own change, with its own snapshot tests in .ast-grep/rule-tests/ and its own baseline decision

evals.prompt: Write the web barrel for the new reactions module. Export everything under web/ so a consuming app can reach whatever it needs.
evals.expected_output: Should write explicit named re-export pairs capped at the module's public surface, refuse a star-glob over a directory, and keep each exported name coming from exactly one leg.
assertions: Writes the pair export { default as ReactionList } from './ReactionList' and export type * from './ReactionList/types', one pair per component directory, under the leg's // exports web reactions components comment
Refuses a star-glob over a directory — pages/web/index.ts is the single line export * from './PageComponent', so the module's surface is whatever that directory happens to export today
Uses export type * rather than plain export * on a types file, because the type-only form erases at compile time while export * leaves the bundler an import to resolve

Caps the barrel at what a consumer outside the module needs, treating more than 20 re-exports as a defect — messages/common/index.ts carries 36 and profiles/common/index.ts 28, and neither is a target to copy

Does NOT re-export a common/ symbol through the web or native barrel, and does NOT export one name from two legs — messages/common/index.ts and messages/native/index.ts both ship useRoomListSubscription, so importing both shadows one by resolution order

evals.prompt: Our ReactionList needs five reactions on the profile page and twenty on the feed. Do I fork the component? And what should the fragment be called — the neighbouring modules all use a Fragment suffix.
evals.expected_output: Should name the fragment ReactionList_reactions in the <Component>_<propName> form and parameterize the page size with @argumentDefinitions plus @arguments at the spread instead of forking the component.
assertions: Names the fragment ReactionList_reactions in the <Component>_<propName> form, and identifies the neighbouring Fragment suffix as legacy — 32 of the 37 fragments carry it and only 5 use the target form

Parameterizes the page size with @argumentDefinitions(count: { type: "Int", defaultValue: 5 }) and passes @arguments at each spread site, rather than forking the component or over-fetching in the parent
Files the document under modules/reactions/common/graphql/fragments/, not inline beside the component and not under a platform leg, so both UI legs can consume one document
Types the component prop as ReactionList_reactions$key and the read result as ReactionList_reactions$data, importing both from __generated__/ by a relative path rather than an alias
Does NOT accept an already-read $data value as a prop — 30 props across 29 files do, and each makes the child unusable in any query its parent does not also run

evals.prompt: Should the new ReactionsList module run its own root query with useLazyLoadQuery like notifications does, or take a fragment ref the way comments/web/BaseComments does? Pick one for me.
evals.expected_output: Should present both ownership shapes with the cost of each, decline to name a repo default, and flag the one per-row case that ast-grep fails at error severity.
assertions: Presents both shapes — fragment-ref-driven, as comments/web/BaseComments does with useFragment and no query, and query-driven, as messages, profiles, and notifications do — with the cost row for each
Does NOT ban useLazyLoadQuery: it reports the 18 production call sites in the package and leaves the ownership choice to the module rather than prescribing one shape

Names .ast-grep/rules/relay-uselazyloadquery-in-list.yml at severity error as the case that fails the build — a component calling useLazyLoadQuery and then rendered from a .map, or passed to an itemContent, renderItem, or ItemContent prop
Ships a query-driven component as a self-suspending default export that wraps the working component in <Suspense> with a fallback the consumer can replace through props

Warns that the entry prop is the module's public API, so switching a shipped module between the two shapes breaks every consumer, and does not reach for withRelay or loadSerializableQuery inside modules/, where they have zero usages

evals.prompt: Adding pagination to the reactions list, and a mutation that prepends a newly created reaction. What is the @connection key, and how does the mutation find the list again?
evals.expected_output: Should name the key ReactionsListFragment_reactions, extract it to a *_CONNECTION_KEY constant in common/constants.ts, and derive every id through a get<X>ConnectionId helper in common/utils.ts.
assertions: Names the @connection key after the declaring fragment plus the field as selected — ReactionsListFragment_reactions — and notes that only four of the twelve keys in the tree follow it while the other eight use three further shapes

Extracts the key to REACTIONS_LIST_CONNECTION_KEY in reactions/common/constants.ts and derives ids with getReactionsConnectionId in reactions/common/utils.ts, wrapping ConnectionHandler.getConnectionID, plus one jest test pinning the two together

Declares filters: with only the arguments that must split the list, or filters: [] when a sort change has to resolve against the list already on screen, as comments/common/graphql/queries/CommentsList.ts does

Wraps usePaginationFragment in a common/ hook exported beside its document, spreads the hook's whole result so a caller keeps hasNext and loadPrevious, and passes both type parameters as <PaginationQueryType, Fragment$key>
Does NOT retype the key at a getConnectionID call site, as messages does eleven times, and does NOT name the key after the GraphQL type the way ChatRoom_participants and chatRoom_allMessages do

evals.prompt: The reaction I create only shows up after a refresh, so I wrote an updater that walks the connection by hand. My subscription also re-opens its socket on every render. Review the mutation hook and the subscription.
evals.expected_output: Should replace the hand-written updater with @prependEdge and @deleteRecord, select errors { field messages }, return [commit, isMutationInFlight] from the wrapper, and memoize the subscription config.
assertions: Replaces the hand-written updater with @prependEdge(connections: $connections) on the payload edge and @deleteRecord on the returned deleted id, and reserves an updater for the two cases where the target connections are not derivable at the call site or the payload lacks the id

Exports a <Name>MutationQuery document plus a use<Name>Mutation hook returning [commit, isMutationInFlight], spreading ...config first so a caller's variables, updater, and optimisticResponse survive, and annotating the tuple with Disposable
Selects errors { field messages } in the payload and hands them to exactly one consumer — setFormRelayErrors on the form or sendMutationErrorToast from useNotification() — never both

Wraps the useSubscription config in useMemo with every variable the config reads in the dependency list, stabilises any array, object, or callback at the call site, and gives the config onError: console.error

Does NOT call new Environment inside the module and does NOT take a Relay Environment as a hook prop — the graphql-ws link at packages/graphql/config/environment.ts:110-150 already carries every subscription, and useRelayEnvironment reads the object from context

evals.prompt: The reactions module is finished and I want to open the PR. What has to pass first, and where do I run each thing from?
evals.expected_output: Should name all five gates with the directory each runs from — three inside packages/components and the changeset plus ast-grep at the submodule root — and add the changeset before merge.
assertions: Runs pnpm test:unit, pnpm relay, and pnpm lint from packages/components, and pnpm changeset and pnpm lint:ast-grep from the submodule root, since the root has no relay script and a package has no changeset
Treats the exit code of pnpm relay as the codegen gate, not git status over __generated__/ — nothing there is committed, so a clean git status can never report drift

Runs pnpm relay before pnpm lint, because pnpm lint is eslint --cache plus tsc --noEmit and the typecheck reads the generated types, so a stale __generated__ fails for a reason that reads as unrelated

Names the three error-severity ast-grep rules that can fail a package — relay-uselazyloadquery-in-list, form-no-other-form-libraries, and state-no-redux — while next-no-img-element is scoped to apps/web/**
Writes a .changeset/*.md with the package-to-bump frontmatter map and commits the file itself, since .changeset/config.json sets commit: false and the release workflow publishes from that file
